5578.problem: Write `makeHeatmap(values)` that maps a list of numeric values (normalized to `[0,1]`) to colors by interpolating through `[blue, cyan, green, yellow, red]` gradient stops.
5578.answer:
func makeHeatmap(values) = {
  local stops = [makeColor([0,0,255]),makeColor([0,255,255]),makeColor([0,255,0]),makeColor([255,255,0]),makeColor([255,0,0])]
  values.map { v ->
    local t = if (v < 0) 0 else if (v > 1) 1 else v
    local seg = floor(t * 4)
    if (seg >= 4) { seg = 3 }
    local lt = t * 4 - seg
    local c1 = splitColor(stops[seg+1])
    local c2 = splitColor(stops[seg+2])
    local r = round(c1[2]*(1-lt)+c2[2]*lt)
    local g = round(c1[3]*(1-lt)+c2[3]*lt)
    local b = round(c1[4]*(1-lt)+c2[4]*lt)
    makeColor([r,g,b])
  }
}
println(makeHeatmap([0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0]))

5395.problem: Write `rotateRight(list, k)` that moves the last `k` elements to the front of the list, equivalent to `rotateLeft(list, list.listLen() - k)`.
5395.answer:
func rotateRight(list, k) = {
  local n = list.listLen()
  local kk = mod(k, n)
  local tail = list.slice(n-kk+1, n)
  local head = list.slice(1, n-kk)
  local result = copyList(tail)
  result.appendList(head)
  result
}
println(rotateRight([1,2,3,4,5], 2))
